reasons: The claimed 'missing behaviour' status is supported: Article IV sets a 36-month Initial Period (renewable at Licensor's option) with exits only for Licensee breach/insolvency, so there is no Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months — a T4C deviation.

The inserted paragraph IV reaches the preferred position with a single minimal addition: Licensee convenience termination on 30 days' written notice, no penalty/early-termination charge, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and express confirmation that Licensor has no convenience right during the committed term. Existing text is left untouched.

The failed deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' is a false negative caused by alias phrasing — the clause uses the contract's defined term 'Licensee' (a Customer alias) rather than 'Customer', which is the correct drafting choice here.

The comment is accurate (correctly characterises the 36-month lock-in and lack of exit), cites the playbook position, offers the 60–90 day / 3-month fee cap fallback, and matches the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
